On current develop (with the #4339 pre-pass) the same replay does not report 18_v10; removing the pre-pass in a test fixture makes it report 18_v10 again.
Comparing a wheel with itself reports zero changes.

The adoption PR body lists changed (platform, benchmark, query) entries, and publish refuses a body that does not equal the list recomputed from the wheels, matching the existing corpus-section check.

description:
Adoption PR #4289 (benchbox-sqlglot 30.31.0.1 to 30.33.0.1) passed full CI, including make sql-execution-gate and the re-recorded golden corpus (bigquery_qualify_17/18), yet changed QuestDB's TPC-H Havoc 18_v10 output. The execution gate emits shipped SQL but executes only on local engines (SQLite, DuckDB, DataFusion, PostgreSQL), so text changes for every other platform go unseen. Upstream 6bff65f6 (#8990) stopped unnesting IN under CASE WHEN; QuestDB rejected the leftover IN subquery ('cannot compare LONG with type CURSOR') in release-v2 44189388601. Platform rewrites run inside translate_sql_query (benchbox/utils/dialect_utils.py), so a diff of that path covers them. A one-off comparison (29,341 queries, 22 benchmarks, 26 dialects, without base_dialect or platform_version) found 9 changed queries including the failing one. Expected outcome: every adoption reports each changed (platform, benchmark, query) translation, and the owner-chosen gate applies to changes on release-gated pairs.

Decision gates (owner, before implementation):
1. Gate semantics, constrained by the owner decisions of 2026-11-17 (sqlglot-adoption-blocked-by-golden-corpus-change-20261117, sqlglot-e2e-first-release-certification: a release certifies only if no person acts between tag and merge): (a) report-only, listing changed queries in the adoption PR body the way corpus changes are listed; (b) report plus an automatic hold label on changes to release-gated pairs, accepting that such a release no longer certifies; (c) another option the owner names.
2. If any acceptance record is chosen, it must fit the single-commit delivery rule (scripts/sqlglot_delivery.py check_adoption_paths), or the owner approves widening it.
3. Placement: extend scripts/sql_execution_gate emission (emit.py) to every dialect, run it inside sqlglot_delivery prepare, or run it as an adoption-PR CI job. A parallel query emitter is not an option.

Guardrails: never execute engines or cloud services for this check; deterministic output (sorted, no timestamps); do not relax or re-record the golden corpus to make it pass; no blanket or glob acknowledgement; use the production adapter path, not a reimplementation; do not weaken the delivery single-commit or ownership checks without explicit owner approval; measure and record runtime before landing.
